headline: Reviewed STAR assessment results, AI and technology guidance, math instruction concerns, and Act 139 compliance; no votes recorded.
summary: Members reviewed first-year STAR assessment results, with about 60% of students proficient overall. They also discussed technology and AI guidance, a new math curriculum, and Act 139 compliance. The minutes record no votes or decisions.
plain_text:
BSD Curriculum Committee Meeting Minutes 
Tuesday, October 27, 2026 at 4:00 PM 
Central Office, 150 Colchester Avenue, Conference Room 1G 
Attendees: Katherine Grykien, Tom Flanagan, Lauren Klaffky, Matthew Price, Gary Golden, Melissa Zygmant 
 
 
1. Opening  
1.1 Call meeting to order 
4:00pm  
1.2 Suspend Robert's Rules 
 
2. Public Comment 
None 
 
3. Discussion  
3.1 Review initial implementation of STAR assessments and results including next steps 
 Grades 1 to 11 took STAR Reading and Math (1st grade took STAR Early Literacy); 
completion rates were very high for a first year 
o Kindergarten will be included in winter testing 
 STAR’s Proficiency benchmarks are 
o Proficiency: 40th percentile  
o Watch: 39th percentile to 25th percentile 
o Intervention: 25th percentile to 10th percentile  
o Urgent Intervention: Below 10th percentile  
 District performance was presented by grade level 
o Overall, approximately 60% of students are proficient across grades and 
schools.  
o There is a larger portion of kids who are below proficiency who are FRL and 
on IEPs  
o The district is about 57% free/reduced lunch 
 High school shows higher at-or-above benchmark rates   
3.2 Updates in technology use and AI guidance 
 Plan has 5 areas: leadership structure, community needs, inventory of current 
tools, finalized AI and EdTech procedures, communications 
 Leadership is split between operations and teaching and learning; Nate and 
Lauren asked to help define a lead 
 Discussion of use of Gemini 
o Discussion of insurance concerns 
Page 1 of 2
Draft
 Discussion of treating general tech use (e.g. iPads, math on computers) separately 
from generative AI policy  
3.3 Math Instruction Concerns 
 Math scores were consistent with state and national scores, but are a point of 
concern for intervention 
 Discussion about the limitations of past instruction 
o Focus on fluency without comprehension  
o Limited effectiveness of comprehension  
 New problem-based curriculum this year  
o Lessons are now better aligned to standards  
3.4 Act 139 Compliance and Interventions 
 District is fully compliant with Act 139 
o Screening extends from K to 11, and parent score letters go to grade 5, 
beyond the K to 3 requirement 
 All K to 5 Tier 3 students have EST plans with targeted goals and one shared 
monitoring tool across 6 schools 
 Screener added Tier 3 students: SA 8, Champlain 10, Flynn monitoring 15, IAA 18  
 K to 3 educators started Stern Center professional learning; middle schools use 
STAR to study Tier 1 trends alongside other data  
3.5 Future Topics 
 Members asked to revisit pathways, proficiency-based learning, and graduation 
requirements; board support likely needed for proficiency grading 
 Sharon Academy invited visitors to see its computer cart model replacing one-to-
one devices  
3.6 Next Steps 
 Review liability insurance policy language to confirm whether AI-related risk is 
covered 
 Settle EdTech and AI leadership in the district  
4. Adjournment 
5:15pm
